title: Filipinos rank among top 3 AI users on messaging platform
summary: Filipinos rank among the top three markets worldwide for artificial intelligence feature usage on Rakuten Viber, according to the messaging platform, with young professionals among the most active…

blocks.text: Filipinos rank among the top three markets worldwide for artificial intelligence feature usage on Rakuten Viber, according to the messaging platform, with young professionals among the most active users of its AI tools.

Viber Chief Product Officer Nadav Melnick said nearly 20% of the platform’s monthly active AI users in the Philippines are aged 25 to 34, followed closely by users aged 35 to 44. The company said the figures reflect growing use of AI for everyday tasks, including finding information, translating messages, summarizing conversations, and drafting replies.

Almost half of AI interactions among Filipino users take place through Viber’s dedicated ChatGPT Tab, where users can ask questions, brainstorm ideas, and seek assistance with daily activities. The Translate feature is another popular tool, alongside Your News, Unread Recap, and AI Reply.

“The strongest adoption is among young professionals and active communicators. These are people balancing work, side hustles, and personal lives,” Melnick said. He added that users were turning to AI because the tools could save time in their daily routines.

As AI becomes more accessible through messaging apps, the information users share with these tools remains an important consideration. Messages can contain personal details, workplace information, financial records, and other sensitive material that users may not intend to share beyond a conversation.

Viber Chief Revenue Officer Cristina Constandache said the company applies its privacy and security principles to its AI integration, including its partnership with OpenAI to bring ChatGPT services to the platform.
Constandache said Viber does not use users’ data to train AI models and that users retain control over whether and how they access its AI features.
“On Viber, AI is never reading user messages passively in the background,” Constandache said, adding that users decide whether to use AI and how much of their data they share with it.

These assurances are relevant as users become accustomed to asking AI tools to process information or generate responses. However, users should still understand what information they submit to an AI feature and how that feature handles it, particularly when working with confidential or sensitive material.

Viber’s Philippine market research, conducted by JTN Research, found that 41% of Filipinos regularly use the platform for work chats, while 46% use it to connect with businesses. The figures underscore the range of personal and professional communications taking place on messaging platforms.

AI adoption is part of a broader pattern of engagement with Viber in the Philippines. Senior Director for Asia-Pacific David Tse said Filipino users spend more time on the app daily than users in other markets, while the company forecasts 16.5% growth in monthly active users in the country.

The Philippines also leads Viber’s markets in several paid and business services. The company reported a 34.3% increase in local ViberPlus subscribers and a 75.5% growth in Philippine contributions to ViberPlus global revenue.

Viber Dating’s average monthly active users in the country grew by 96.9%, compared with a global average of 44%, according to the company. Filipino users also account for 56% of new profiles on the service.

Businesses are another part of the platform’s local growth. The Philippines accounts for 24% of Viber’s global live business accounts, with the company reporting a 20.5% increase in live accounts and 127.3% growth in meaningful business interactions.

Viber also plans to work with the Department of Tourism to help travelers discover accredited tourism businesses through Viber Business Accounts and Marketplace. The proposed partnership aims to give tourism-related micro, small, and medium enterprises another way to reach customers while helping visitors find legitimate businesses.

The company’s growing range of services reflects how messaging platforms are expanding beyond personal communication. As AI features become part of that ecosystem, their usefulness will depend not only on how easily people can access them, but also on whether users understand their capabilities and the privacy considerations involved in using them
